t.7.23.1: Having conquered Yama, the foremost of the gods, the ten-necked Rāvaṇa, boasting of his victory, then looked upon his own companions.
t.7.23.2: Then all of them, led by Mārīca, having hailed him with cries of victory and been reassured by Rāvaṇa, boarded the Puṣpaka.
t.7.23.4: He, having gone to the city Bhogavatī, protected by Vāsuki, and having established the Nāgas under his control, then went on to the city Maṇimatī.
t.7.23.3: Then, delighted, he entered Rasātala, the ocean, that treasure-house of waters, inhabited by hosts of Daityas and serpents and well guarded by Varuṇa.
t.7.23.5: There dwelt the Daityas called the Nivātakavacas, who had obtained boons. The Rākṣasa approached them and challenged them to battle.
t.7.23.6: But all those Daiteyas, exceedingly valorous and endowed with great strength, bearing various weapons and mad for battle, fought fiercely there.
t.7.23.7: While they were fighting, more than a full year passed, and there was neither victory nor destruction for either of the two.
t.7.23.8: Then the Grandsire, the imperishable god who is the refuge of the three worlds, came there swiftly, mounted on the finest of aerial chariots.
t.7.23.9: Having halted that battle of the Nivātakavacas, the aged Pitāmaha spoke words like one to whom the matter was fully known.
t.7.23.10: For this Rāvaṇa cannot be conquered in battle by the gods and asuras, nor can you be brought to destruction by the gods and asuras together with Indra.
t.7.23.12: Then Rāvaṇa made there a friendship with the Nivātakavacas, with Agni as witness, and at that time he became filled with joy.
t.7.23.11: Friendship between the rākṣasa and you is indeed pleasing, for among friends all interests are held undivided; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.23.13: Honored by them in due fashion, Daśānana dwelt there happily for a year, and he received worship no different from that in his own city.
t.7.23.14: Having mastered ninety-nine magical arts, he, self-possessed, roamed through Rasātala in search of the city of the lord of the waters.
t.7.23.15: Then, reaching the city named Aśmanagara, guarded by the Kālakeyas, he conquered it within a moment and slew four hundred Daityas.
t.7.23.16: Then the lord of the Rākṣasas beheld the divine abode of Varuṇa, gleaming like a pale white cloud and standing firm like Mount Kailāsa.
t.7.23.17: He beheld Surabhi, the cow, standing there and ever streaming milk, from whose outflow of milk arose the ocean named Kṣīroda.
t.7.23.18: It is that from which the cool-rayed moon arises, beneficial to all creatures; that by resorting to which the supreme sages who drink foam sustain their lives; and that in which the nectar of immortality was born, and also surā, the wine of the wine-drinkers.
t.7.23.19: Having circumambulated that most wondrous cow whom men in the world call by the name Surabhi, Rāvaṇa entered the exceedingly dreadful abode, guarded by forces of many kinds.
t.7.23.20: Then he beheld the excellent abode of Varuṇa, strewn with hundreds of streams, resembling an autumn cloud and ever joyful.
t.7.23.21: Then, having slain the commanders of the army in battle, though he himself had been struck by them, he said: "Where has he gone who is your king? Let it be told at once!"
t.7.23.22: Rāvaṇa has come seeking battle; let battle be given to him. Or else, with joined palms, say, “I am defeated,” and you will have nothing to fear.
t.7.23.23: Meanwhile, the enraged sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuṇa came forth, and Gau too, who dwelt in Puṣkara.
t.7.23.25: Then there arose a fierce, hair-raising battle between the sons of the lord of the waters and the Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa.
t.7.23.24: But they, endowed with valour and excellent qualities, surrounded by their own forces and shining with the splendour of the rising sun, yoked their chariots that went wherever they willed.
t.7.23.26: But by the mighty ministers of the Rākṣasa Daśagrīva, that entire army of Varuṇa was struck down in a moment.
t.7.23.27: Then the sons of Varuṇa, seeing their own army in the battle and themselves tormented by a net of arrows, withdrew from the work of combat.
t.7.23.28: But they, who had been standing on the surface of the earth, seeing Rāvaṇa in the Puṣpaka, swiftly entered the sky in their fast-moving chariots.
t.7.23.29: Then, having reached that equal footing, there arose among them a great and tumultuous battle in the sky, like that between a god and a Dānava.
t.7.23.30: Then, having turned Rāvaṇa back in battle with arrows resembling fire, they, greatly delighted, roared out cries of many kinds.
t.7.23.31: Then the heroic Mahodara, enraged at seeing his king overpowered, cast off all fear of death and, eager for battle, looked about him.
t.7.23.32: And their horses, which went wherever they willed and were swift as the wind, were struck down by that Mahodara with his mace and fell to the earth.
t.7.23.33: Having slain the warriors and those horses of the sons of Varuṇa, and seeing them standing there deprived of their chariots, he swiftly let out a mighty roar.
t.7.23.34: But those chariots of theirs, together with their horses and their excellent charioteers, were struck down by Mahodara and fell upon the surface of the earth.
t.7.23.35: But the sons of the great-souled Varuṇa, those heroes, abandoning their chariots, stood firm in the sky and, by virtue of their own power, were not distressed.
t.7.23.36: Having strung their bows and pierced Mahodara through, they, enraged and united, rushed together upon Rāvaṇa in battle.
t.7.23.37: Then the enraged Daśagrīva, standing firm like the fire of universal destruction, let fall a shower of arrows of great velocity upon their vital parts.
t.7.23.38: Then the unassailable one, stationed above them, rained down upon them variegated maces and hundreds of arrows, as well as axes, spears, śataghnīs and lances.
t.7.23.39: Then those heroes, pierced with wounds, rushed forth on foot.
t.7.23.40: Then the Rākṣasa, letting out a mighty roar, struck down the sons of Varuṇa with many kinds of terrible weapons, as a cloud strikes with torrents of rain.
t.7.23.41: Then all of them, turned away from the fight and fallen upon the surface of the earth, were swiftly carried from the battlefield by their own men and brought back to their homes.
t.7.23.42: Then the rākṣasa said to them, "Let Varuṇa be informed." And Varuṇa's minister, named Prabhāsa, spoke to Rāvaṇa.
t.7.23.43: Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, of great splendor, whom you summon to battle, has indeed gone to Brahmaloka to hear the music of the Gandharvas.
t.7.23.45: But the lord of the Rākṣasas, having heard that and having proclaimed his own name, let out a roar of delight and went forth from the abode of Varuṇa.
t.7.23.44: What then is gained, O hero, by your exerting yourself in vain, now that the king has gone away? The heroic princes who were present here have been defeated.
t.7.23.46: Turning back by the very path by which he had come, that Rākṣasa, moving through the expanse of the sky, went on with his face turned toward Laṅkā.
